proposed_statement_changes.reason: For a finite signed measure, finite means finite total variation and does not imply finite support. The risk inequality and existence hold at that generality, but an exact finite linear program is available only after the signed input itself has finite support, such as after the quantization already contemplated by the estimator construction.

proposed_core_edits.reason: The proof constructs the complete causal witness law and performs a fixed-sample minimax reduction, so the dependency metadata must expose the target-law definitions and the sampling, normalization, design, consistency, and ignorability premises used in those steps.

proposed.justification: This is the first same-class obstruction that can make marginal transport strictly harder than both direct density estimation and a scalar missing-response functional.
proposed.gap: LuedtkeFukumizu2025DoubleGen imports an oracle lower bound and explicitly says it may be loose for nonsmooth nuisances; even after fixing the covariate law to be known uniform, that paper gives no difficulty-sensitive transport converse, while KennedyEtAl2024MinimaxCATE has a scalar or pointwise fuzzy hypothesis rather than separation for an entire marginal law.
proposed.consumer: The result gives DoubleGen and DecFM a known-uniform-design stress-test benchmark showing when generator capacity cannot remove observational indistinguishability caused by rough shared nuisances even before unknown-design difficulty is introduced.

proposed_core_edits.reason: The narrowed computational clause also exposes Kantorovich--Rubinstein duality as a load-bearing cited dependency.

proposed.justification: Higher-order coefficient correction can be signed, so an order-preserving projection theorem is needed to deliver an actual generative distribution.
proposed.gap: NilesWeedBerthet2022 projects direct-sample wavelet estimates to densities or discrete measures; the present statement isolates a finite-grid signed-input oracle inequality suitable after causal higher-order correction.
proposed.consumer: The known-design reconstruction benchmark can return probability masses and sample categorically without clipping away multiscale cancellation.

proposed_core_edits.reason: The upper half of the oracle benchmark uses the published bounded-density Besov wavelet theorem, while the proof supplies the Hölder-to-Besov transfer and a direct Hölder packing for the converse.

proposed.justification: This reduction is the mandatory sanity check for the phase diagram and pins the baseline that rough nuisances may or may not exceed.
proposed.gap: NilesWeedBerthet2022 proves the direct-sample rate over positive Besov density classes; the proposition requires the same exponent on the present classical Hölder benchmark and embeds that direct experiment as a randomized no-covariate-variation submodel.
proposed.consumer: It certifies that the known-design correction does not lose rate when the benchmark experiment becomes an oracle generation problem.

open_obligations.what_is_open: A joint nonasymptotic negative-Besov risk bound for all retained outcome coefficients when the scale-dependent covariate rank exceeds the sample size.
open_obligations.obstruction: The full-rank finite-order degenerate correction has covariance contractions with positive powers of rank divided by sample size. The frozen class supplies neither mixed covariate-outcome smoothness nor spectral decay, and deterministic inverse-remainder control does not bound these stochastic contractions. Assuming the desired certificate would assume the crux of the OEQ.
open_obligations.attempted: Expanded the sign-mixture lower experiment exactly, isolated the two higher-order likelihood terms, and closed probability reconstruction from any signed coefficient bound. For the upper construction, examined the direct finite-order Neumann correction; its high-rank degenerate terms do not yield a uniform summable bound by the available sectional Hölder estimates.

open_obligations.what_is_open: The matching achievability rate and all-regime converse, including critical logarithms and the asymmetric regime in which the shared-propensity leakage term dominates.
open_obligations.obstruction: The interaction lower envelope is rigorous, but matching it requires the unresolved high-rank coefficient certificate or a different estimator. Conversely, the present shared-sign mixture alone does not certify every asymmetric regime or any critical multiscale logarithm. No honest optimization of unproved coefficient bounds can determine the sharp frontier.
open_obligations.attempted: Derived the full shared-sign mixture calculation, the representative strict separation, the oracle submodel rate, and the signed-to-probability projection. Also optimized an explicit clipped propensity-series inverse-weighted estimator to obtain a loose same-class upper rate; this does not exploit outcome smoothness and therefore does not match the lower side in general.
